question.text: Per the current NISM XVII workbook, which of the following correctly describes Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) already issued and outstanding, compared with physical gold?

answer.text: SGBs carry no price risk because returns are guaranteed by the RBI

Already-issued SGBs paid an additional interest of 2.50% per annum (semi-annually) on the initial investment over and above gold-price appreciation, and had an 8-year tenor; fresh SGB issuance has been discontinued from FY 2024-25 per the workbook
SGBs can be stored in a bank locker, just like physical gold
SGBs have no lock-in period and can be redeemed anytime

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM XVII workbook supports the 2.50% p.a. additional interest and 8-year tenor for SGBs that were issued. It also notes that fresh SGB issuance is discontinued from FY 2024-25. SGBs continue to carry gold-price risk; they are not guaranteed in price terms. The Trap: Options A, C, and D misstate basic SGB features. Any unqualified claim that "SGBs are available for new issuance" is inconsistent with the current workbook. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XVII and V-A both reference SGB features and the FY 2024-25 discontinuation of fresh issuance.
